title: Canadian Police Arrest Suspect Seven Months After Indian-Origin Woman Himanshi Khurana Murdered in Toronto
excerpt: Abdul Ghafoori, 32, faces first-degree murder charges after a Canada-wide manhunt following the December 2025 killing classified as intimate partner violence.
body:
• Abdul Ghafoori, 32, has been arrested by Canadian police approximately seven months after the murder of his Indian-origin partner Himanshi Khurana, 30, in Toronto.
  • Khurana was found dead inside a residence near Strachan Avenue and Wellington Street West on December 20, 2025, after a missing person report was filed the previous night.
  • Toronto Police classified the case as intimate partner violence and issued a Canada-wide warrant for Ghafoori on charges of first-degree murder.
  • The Indian Consulate General in Toronto had provided assistance to Khurana's family and coordinated with Canadian authorities throughout the investigation.

Seven-Month Manhunt Ends in Arrest

Canadian police have arrested Abdul Ghafoori, 32, the man wanted for the murder of Indian-origin woman Himanshi Khurana in Toronto, bringing a seven-month manhunt to a close. Ghafoori had been the subject of a Canada-wide warrant for first-degree murder since December 2025, according to the Toronto Police Service.

https://x.com/dna/status/2086345370737778813

Khurana, a 30-year-old Indian national living in Toronto, was found dead inside a residence near Strachan Avenue and Wellington Street West on December 20, 2025. Police had responded to a missing person report filed late the previous evening and located her body early the following morning.

Investigators identified the case as an act of intimate partner violence. Toronto police confirmed that Khurana and Ghafoori had been in a relationship prior to her death.

How the Investigation Unfolded

The timeline of events began on the evening of December 19, 2025, when Toronto police received a report of a missing woman in the Strachan Avenue area at approximately 10:41 p.m. Officers searched through the night, and by 6:30 a.m. the next morning, they discovered Khurana's body inside a residence.

The death was classified as a homicide — Toronto's 40th of 2025, according to police records. Within days, investigators named Ghafoori as the suspect and issued an arrest warrant. Police released his photograph and appealed to the public for help locating him.

"We have released an image of the suspect, and that is out there, and we're appealing to the public, if anybody would happen to know where this man is to please call police," a Toronto Police spokesperson said at the time.

India's Diplomatic Response

The Indian Consulate General in Toronto responded swiftly to the case. In a post on X in December, the consulate stated: "We are deeply saddened and shocked by the murder of Ms. Himanshi Khurana, a young Indian national, in Toronto. We extend our deepest condolences to her bereaved family during this moment of profound grief."

The consulate confirmed it had been "in close touch with the matter" and was providing "all possible assistance" to Khurana's family in coordination with Canadian authorities. The diplomatic intervention highlighted the growing concern over the safety of Indian nationals in Canada, a country that hosts one of the largest Indian diaspora populations in the world.

Intimate Partner Violence in the Diaspora

The case has drawn renewed attention to the issue of intimate partner violence within immigrant communities in Canada. Advocacy groups have long pointed out that new immigrants — particularly women on dependent visas or those without strong local support networks — face heightened vulnerability in abusive relationships.

According to Canadian government data, intimate partner violence accounts for roughly one in four police-reported violent crimes in the country. Community organizations serving South Asian populations in the Greater Toronto Area have called for expanded culturally sensitive support services, including multilingual crisis lines and immigration-status-independent shelter access.

What Happens Next

Ghafoori faces a charge of first-degree murder, which carries a mandatory sentence of life imprisonment with no eligibility for parole for 25 years if convicted. The case will proceed through the Ontario court system. Specific details about the circumstances of his arrest, including where and how he was apprehended after seven months on the run, are expected to emerge as court proceedings begin.

For Khurana's family, the arrest offers a measure of accountability after months of uncertainty. The Indian consulate has confirmed it will continue to support the family through the legal process ahead.
